description: What the same map would cost, without making it. Free, and refused by the same guards a real call meets. Bandwidth is priced per megabyte because nobody knows a site's sitemap size before reading it.

includeSubdomains.description: Also keep URLs on other hosts of the same domain, like `blog.example.com` for `example.com`. Off by default: only the host you named, with or without `www.`.

limit.description: How many URLs to hand back at most, 1 to 30,000. The price is the same whatever you ask for.

proxy.description: Where the map's requests leave from. Every file it reads goes through the same exit.

country.description: Where the call should look like it comes from, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (`us`, `br`). Name one and the managed pool leaves from that country. Leave it out and the page sees a US browser, from an address we pick. A scrape or a map on the managed pool makes one exception: a site whose address ends in `.br`, `.de`, `.es`, `.fr`, `.it`, `.jp`, `.nl`, `.pl` or `.uk` is read from its own country. The browser's clock and languages follow the country on every pool.

pool.description: Which exit to leave through. "residential" is the managed pool, metered by the megabyte; "custom" is your own proxy, free on every plan, bytes never billed.

server.description: Your own proxy, `http(s)://[user:pass@]host:port`. Required for pool "custom", refused for the managed one.

search.description: Only URLs that contain this text, upper or lower case alike: `blog` keeps `/blog/` and `/Blog-post`.

sitemap.description: Where to look. "include" reads the site's sitemaps and the links on the page you named; "only" reads the sitemaps alone; "skip" reads the page's links alone.

url.description: The site to map, as any http(s) URL on it. Private and loopback hosts are refused.
